transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um, well, I hope I'm in the right place for this. It’s probably just a small thing, really, maybe just a quirk of getting older, but... well, I help out at the local museum, and I’ve been noticing that people will be talking right to me—maybe explaining the details for the next art walk or something like that—and I’ll be looking right at them, but then... I suddenly realize I completely missed the middle of what they said. 

It’s a little embarrassing, honestly. I have to ask them to run it by me again, even though I was standing right there the whole time. I always try to play it off politely so I don't seem rude, but... I don't know, does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing you usually help people with?

```json
{"intent": "Determine whether the lapses are due to active mind-wandering/distraction or sudden blank episodes of lost awareness.", "question": "During those moments when you miss what

Oh, um... what I'm thinking about, you mean? That's a really good question, Doctor. I'm... I'm actually not entirely sure. 

I suppose I don't really realize what's happening until the exact moment I notice I've tuned out. It's probably just me being a little silly, you know? Maybe my mind just drifts off for a second, or I get a bit distracted by one of the displays behind them. I don't know if my mind goes completely blank, but I couldn't tell you exactly what I was thinking about either. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just haven't paid close enough attention to the... the mechanics of it, I guess. Does that sound like normal daydreaming to you?

```json
{"intent": "Determine whether the patient is responsive or exhibits observable automatisms during these episodes.", "question": "Has anyone ever told you that you were unresponsive, stared blankly, or

Oh, no, no one has ever said anything like that to me. I'm pretty sure I don't just stare off into space like a statue or anything alarming. 

I always try to nod along and make polite noises, you know? So I think I look like I'm listening, even if I've missed a little bit of the conversation. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was ignoring them on purpose. It's really just a momentary lapse, I think. I hope that makes sense? I'm sure it's nothing too serious, right?
Did you experience similar difficulties with paying attention or staying focused back when you were a child in school?

Well, um... I suppose so, yes. But I think that's just how kids are, right? I mean, I wasn't a bad student or anything, I promise. I never caused any trouble in class. 

But, well, if I'm being completely honest... I do remember my report cards from back in grade school usually had little notes from the teachers. Things like, um, "daydreams a lot" or "needs reminders to finish his work." Just typical boy stuff, I always figured. And my mother... well, she was wonderful, but she did have to sit right next to me at the kitchen table to make sure I actually finished my homework. At least until I was about twelve or so. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was lazy! I really did try my best, I just... my mind would wander a bit, I guess. Is that the kind of thing you're looking for, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right information.
Outside of conversations, do you often find it difficult to stay organized or keep track of your belongings and daily tasks?

Well, um... I really do try my best to keep things in order. I wouldn't want you to think I'm completely disorganized or living in a mess, I promise. 

But, oh dear, if I'm being perfectly honest... I suppose I do have a bit of a silly habit of misplacing my things. Like, um, I'll be helping out and I'll put down the camera battery, or maybe the name tags, or... or the envelope with the sign-up sheets. I always tell myself I'm putting them somewhere very safe! But then, well, I end up spending half the morning just retracing my steps trying to find them again. 

It's a bit embarrassing to admit, to be honest with you. But that's just normal forgetfulness, isn't it? I mean, everyone misplaces things now and then, especially at my age... right? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is. I really do try to keep track of it all.
